clue.text: Living quarters round a royal residence

indicators.note: one word going round another wraps it, so the second sits inside the first

parts.note: your place is where you live

explanation.surface: Staff accommodation built around a royal home.
explanation.walkthrough: PLACE wraps A to make PALACE. 'Living quarters' looks like part of the royal picture but is the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: A palace is the official home of a monarch, a royal dwelling.

clue.text: Seen from 13, perhaps, in harbour, copper is checking lines

indicators.note: to check something is to hold it back, so these letters hem in what follows

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
L is the abbreviation for line, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A policeman stands in a harbour, keeping an eye on the queues of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is DRAWBRIDGE; someone crossing one looks straight at the portcullis. 'copper' is a policeman in the surface but the chemical element in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A portcullis is the iron grating dropped over a castle gateway, typically right behind the drawbridge, so it is an example of what 13 reveals.

clue.text: Rope in young woman, opposed at first

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the preceding word is wanted

explanation.surface: Someone tries to rope a reluctant young woman into a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rope in' reads as one phrase meaning persuade, but 'Rope' alone is the definition and 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a rope with a running noose used by cowboys to catch cattle.

clue.text: Eat whole amount in wafer

indicators.note: something in something else sits inside it

parts.note: an ice-cream cone is a wafer

explanation.surface: An instruction to eat the entire filling of a wafer.
explanation.walkthrough: The wafer is not a biscuit here but the edible cone that holds ice cream.
explanation.definitionFit: To consume food is to eat it up; the verb is a more formal synonym.

clue.text: Musician having grand spot close to microphone in pub

indicators.note: the material before this word goes inside the word after it

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
a pip is a spot, as on dice or cards

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter is kept

explanation.surface: A performer gets a big slot by the mic at the local pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A grand is British slang for a thousand pounds, abbreviated G.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagpiper is a player of the bagpipes, so a kind of musician.

clue.text: Everyone amazed, reportedly, over effort accepted as part of normal routine

definitions.text: accepted as part of normal routine

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than read, so the sound matters, not the spelling

parts.note: someone amazed is in a daze, which is said like these words

explanation.surface: Everybody is said to be stunned by an effort that turned out to be routine.
explanation.walkthrough: IN A DAZE is said just like IN A DAY'S, giving ALL + IN A DAY'S + WORK.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'all in a day's work' describes something unremarkable that comes with the job.

clue.text: A hot spice dad and I got in park abroad

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so this letter goes inside
something abroad is out of its usual place, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: Father and I picked up a fiery seasoning in a park overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter I goes into the middle of the rearranged park, not into the dad.
explanation.definitionFit: Paprika is a powdered red pepper seasoning, and some varieties are hot.

clue.text: Clerk in stall with drug dealer

parts.note: a stall for animals is a pen

explanation.surface: An office worker shares a market stall with someone dealing drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the two parts: PEN + PUSHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen-pusher is a disparaging name for an office clerk who does routine paperwork.

clue.text: Not quite willing to study

indicators.note: not quite all of the word is used, so its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone is only half-keen to get down to studying.
explanation.walkthrough: READY without its final Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a subject at university is to study it, a British usage.

clue.text: Article on wonderful revolution in British society

parts.note: a revolution is a full turn, a circle

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about a marvellous upheaval in British social life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests political upheaval, but it is a turn round a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magic Circle is the London-based organisation of professional conjurors, a British society.

clue.text: Playwright's role hasn't changed

indicators.note: the letters are changed round into a new order

explanation.surface: A dramatist's part in the play has stayed the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't changed' reads as no change at all, yet changed is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Rosenthal was an English writer of television plays such as The Barmitzvah Boy.

clue.text: Raccoon-like animal in Japan, dangerous

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: spans the end of Japan and the start of dangerous

explanation.surface: A warning about a raccoon-like creature in Japan being dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: Hidden across japAN DAngerous with the P from Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: The red panda resembles a raccoon, and was once classed in the raccoon family.

clue.text: A toasted sandwich and rice our mosque unexpectedly produced around noon

indicators.note: the reworked letters go around the one that follows
something produced unexpectedly comes out in a surprising form, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A lunchtime surprise: rice and a toastie served at a mosque at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: Noon supplies only its abbreviation, N, which the shuffled letters surround.
explanation.definitionFit: A croque-monsieur is the French grilled ham and cheese sandwich.

clue.text: To tie game this may have been deployed in defence

definitions.text: this may have been deployed in defence

parts.note: a tied match is a draw

explanation.surface: A football manager explains a defensive tactic used to secure a tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed in defence' sounds like football tactics, but the defence is a castle's.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawbridge is a hinged bridge over a moat, raised to keep attackers out of a castle.

clue.text: Conservative entering draw for money

indicators.note: something entering another goes inside it

parts.note: to draw in is to lure

explanation.surface: A Tory joins a raffle hoping to win some cash.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside LURE: LU-C-RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money, usually with a hint of greed, as in 'filthy lucre'.

clue.text: Record, a minute about proposal made to get a watertight structure

indicators.note: about means around, so the earlier letters go around the next word

parts.note: a compact disc is a record

explanation.surface: Minutes are taken of a proposal meant to obtain a watertight deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' acts only on the record, which splits around the proposal; the a and minute follow on afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A cofferdam is an enclosure pumped dry so that building work can be done below the waterline.

clue.text: Sponsor of daughter university rejected, surprisingly

indicators.note: the remaining letters turn up in a surprising order
what is rejected is thrown out, so that letter is removed

explanation.surface: A daughter's backer is surprised when her university application fails.
explanation.walkthrough: OF DAUGHTER loses U, and the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: At a christening a godfather stands sponsor for the child, vouching for their religious upbringing.

clue.text: Hotly pursuing filly, run unwisely having caught cold

indicators.note: catching something means holding it inside
something done unwisely goes wrong, so the letters fall out of order

parts.note: C is short for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A young racehorse chasing hard runs recklessly and catches a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: FILLY RUN rearranged, holding C.
explanation.definitionFit: Hounds in full cry are baying as they chase the quarry, so the idiom means in hot pursuit.

clue.text: Spectacles — girl has lost a good number inside

indicators.note: the preceding letters are placed within the shortened name
losing something means it is taken away, so that letter goes

parts.note: no. is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: Glasses: a girl has mislaid a good many of them inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a good number' looks like 'many' but splits three ways: the a is what the girl loses, and good and number go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorgnon is a pair of eyeglasses or opera glasses held up by a handle.

clue.text: Sprinkle right into casserole

indicators.note: putting one thing into another places it inside

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction to scatter something straight into the stew pot.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes into STEW: ST-R-EW.
explanation.definitionFit: To strew is to scatter or sprinkle things over a surface.

clue.text: Go round, check about a vegetable

parts.note: to spin is to go round
ch is the chess notation for check

explanation.surface: Instructions to circle back and check on a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' here means next to rather than around, so nothing is wrapped; chess players write check as ch.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy green plant eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Use this when driving off at first?

definitions.meaning: surface reading: advice about pulling away from the kerb in a car
setter's reading: before setting off you look at what is behind you, the reflected view backwards

explanation.walkthrough: The driving-lesson rule is mirror, signal, manoeuvre: the first thing you do before pulling off is check behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The interior glass above the windscreen lets a driver see traffic behind before moving out.

clue.text: King, say — one responsible for a line?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a monarch or sovereign who reigns
second meaning: the straight-edged stick used to draw a straight line

explanation.surface: A monarch might be the one accountable for a royal line of succession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a line' suggests a dynasty, which fits a king; but the second sense is the drawing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A king is one kind of sovereign who governs; the stationery item is what draws pencil lines straight.

clue.text: Short publisher's puff leaves a confused impression

indicators.note: cutting a word short trims its final letter

parts.note: a blurb is the promotional text a publisher puts on a book

explanation.surface: A brief bit of publisher's hype leaves readers muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: BLURB loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A blur is something seen or remembered indistinctly, a hazy impression.

clue.text: Loaded in large Yemeni port

parts.note: Aden is a port city in Yemen

explanation.surface: Ships are loaded up at a big harbour in Yemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' reads as a container signal, but here it simply joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means carrying a heavy load, a synonym of loaded.

clue.text: Troubled by brief that's limited

parts.note: ailed means troubled, as in 'what ailed him'

explanation.surface: Someone is bothered by a short memo that restricts them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troubled' looks like an anagram signal but supplies a word: CURT placed by AILED.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtailed means cut short or restricted, which is to be limited.

clue.text: Aide-memoire concerning bodyguard

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A memo note on the subject of a security guard.
explanation.walkthrough: RE + MINDER.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide-memoire is a note to jog the memory, which is what a reminder does.

clue.text: Terrible rage after child makes accusation

indicators.note: coming after means following, so the reworked word is placed second behind the other piece

parts.note: ch is the abbreviation for child

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A terrible tantrum following a child's behaviour leads to someone being blamed.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the rage first, but 'after' puts it behind the child in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge is a formal accusation of an offence.
